newsitem.title: ITALY: Eleven held in Mafia swoop in Sicily.
newsitem.headline: Eleven held in Mafia swoop in Sicily.

text.p: Police arrested 11 people in the Sicilian capital Palermo on Tuesday in dawn raids on businessmen suspected of having links with the Mafia.

Police said the 11, and a 12th suspect still being sought, were alleged to have run building companies and other firms set up by the Mafia to recycle money gleaned from robberies and protection rackets.
They included a former senior local health official, Antonino Rizzuto, 71, who was granted permission to be held under house arrest.

Italian media reported that the arrests followed testimony from Mob turncoats. These included self-confessed killer Salvatore Cucuzza, 50, who controlled central Palermo for the Corleonesi clan of arrested "boss of bosses" Salvatore Riina until his capture last May.
Cucuzza has since told police that he took part in several killings, including the murder in 1982 of the leader of the Italian Communist Party in Sicily, Pio La Torre.
Italy has scored significant successes in recent years in its crackdown on the Mafia, with the arrests of Riina and other leading members held responsible for a series of killings.

Investigators say, however, that the state has yet to make similar significant inroads into the web of economic power organised crime wields through money laundering and other illegal financial activities.
